papers.title: Improved Mechanical Properties and Energy Absorption of BCC Lattice Structures with Triply Periodic Minimal Surfaces Fabricated by SLM
papers.abstract: The triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) method is a novel approach for lattice design in a range of fields, such as impact protection and structural lightweighting. In this paper, we used the TPMS formula to rapidly and accurately generate the most common lattice structure, named the body centered cubic (BCC) structure, with certain volume fractions. TPMS-based and computer aided design (CAD) based BCC lattice structures with volume fractions in the range of 10⁻30% were fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM) technology with Ti⁻6Al⁻4V and subjected to compressive tests. The results demonstrated that local geometric features changed the volume and stress distributions, revealing that the TPMS-based samples were superior to the CAD-based ones, with elastic modulus, yield strength and compression strength increasing in the ranges of 18.9⁻42.2%, 19.2⁻29.5%, and 2⁻36.6%, respectively. The failure mechanism of the TPMS-based samples with a high volume fraction changed to brittle failure observed by scanning electron microscope (SEM), as their struts were more affected by the axial force and fractured on struts. It was also found that the TPMS-based samples have a favorable capacity to absorb energy, particularly with a 30% volume fraction, the energy absorbed up to 50% strain was approximately three times higher than that of the CAD-based sample with an equal volume fraction. Furthermore, the theoretic Gibson⁻Ashby mode was established in order to predict and design the mechanical properties of the lattice structures. In summary, these results can be used to rapidly create BCC lattice structures with superior compressive properties for engineering applications.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索TPMS方法设计BCC点阵结构以改善力学性能与能量吸收。
summary_zh.method: 通过SLM制造TPMS与CAD两种BCC点阵并比较其压缩行为。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the use of triply periodic minimal surfaces (TPMS) for designing BCC lattice structures with improved mechanical properties and energy absorption.
summary_en.method: BCC lattice structures with varying volume fractions were fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM) using Ti-6Al-4V, comparing TPMS-based and CAD-based designs under compression.
summary_en.result: TPMS-based lattices exhibited up to 42.2% increase in elastic modulus, 29.5% in yield strength, and 36.6% in compression strength, with superior energy absorption at 30% volume fraction.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical Gibson-Ashby model was established and validated through experimental compression tests and SEM fractography.

papers.title: Refining the Microstructure of Fe‐Nd‐B by Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: Lab scale additive manufacturing of Fe‐Nd‐B based permanent magnet material (Fe75‐Nd18‐B7) has been performed. For fabrication a special inert gas process chamber for laser powder bed fusion has been used. This is required because Fe‐Nd‐B powders are extremely sensitive to oxidation. Selective laser melting (SLM) of the powders allows to realize very fine microstructures with a directed crystal growth and finely dispersed Nd‐rich phase. It is shown, that this fine and textured microstructure leads to large coercivity in sintered Fe‐Nd‐B magnets. A prototype has been realized by milling the SLM alloy and sintering.

llm.why_not_core: The paper is about magnetic material fabrication (Fe-Nd-B magnets) using SLM, with no biomedical implant context, no stress shielding analysis, no mechanical testing for implants, and no fatigue or osseointegration evaluation.

summary_zh.motivation: 利用选区激光熔化制备具有精细微观结构的Fe-Nd-B永磁材料。
summary_zh.method: 采用惰性气体氛围的激光粉末床熔融工艺，并进行后续烧结处理。
summary_zh.result: 精细定向的微观结构显著提高了磁体的矫顽力。
summary_zh.validation: 通过微观结构分析和磁性能测量进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate Fe-Nd-B permanent magnets with fine and textured microstructures using selective laser melting to enhance magnetic coercivity.
summary_en.method: Powder bed fusion under inert atmosphere was used to melt Fe75-Nd18-B7 powder, followed by milling and sintering to produce a prototype magnet.
summary_en.result: The SLM-processed alloy exhibited a fine, textured microstructure with dispersed Nd-rich phase, leading to high coercivity compared to conventional sintered magnets.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural characterization (SEM, XRD) and magnetic property measurements (coercivity, remanence) were performed to confirm the refined microstructure and enhanced magnetic performance.
